books.title: The Cost of Discipleship
books.subtitle: Reflections on the Sermon on the Mount
books.author: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
books.description: A reflection on the Sermon on the Mount that explores the distinction between cheap grace and costly grace, and what Bonhoeffer understood as the demands of following Jesus.
books.longDescription: Dietrich Bonhoeffer wrote this work in 1937 while living under the Nazi regime in Germany. Drawing on the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5–7), he examines what it means to follow Jesus, arguing that grace is not a possession to be used but a call to be obeyed. The book is divided into two parts: an extended meditation on the Sermon on the Mount and a section on the concrete demands of discipleship. It has been widely read within Lutheran, Reformed, and ecumenical traditions.

books.title: Mere Christianity
books.author: C.S. Lewis
books.description: An apologetic work compiled from C.S. Lewis's BBC radio broadcasts during World War II, examining the foundations of Christian belief from a lay perspective.
books.longDescription: C.S. Lewis delivered these talks on BBC radio between 1941 and 1944. The book is organized into four parts: the case for Christian morality, the problem of human nature, Christian behavior, and the theological virtues. Lewis writes as a layperson addressing other laypeople, drawing on philosophy and everyday reasoning rather than technical theology. The work has been read widely across Protestant and Catholic traditions.

books.title: Confessions
books.author: Augustine of Hippo
books.edition: Penguin Classics edition, translated by Henry Chadwick, 1991
books.description: Augustine's autobiographical account of his early life, conversion, and theological reflection, written in the late fourth century.
books.longDescription: Augustine of Hippo composed the Confessions around 397–400 AD. The work is divided into thirteen books: the first ten recount his life from childhood through his conversion, and the last three offer a theological commentary on Genesis 1. Written in the form of a prayer addressed to God, the Confessions is among the earliest surviving autobiographies in Western literature. It has been influential across Catholic, Reformed, Lutheran, and Orthodox traditions.

books.title: The Pilgrim's Progress
books.subtitle: From This World to That Which Is to Come
books.author: John Bunyan
books.description: An allegorical narrative depicting the journey of a man called Christian from the City of Destruction to the Celestial City.
books.longDescription: John Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim's Progress during his imprisonment for nonconformist preaching. Published in 1678, it follows the character Christian through locations such as the Slough of Despond, Vanity Fair, and the Valley of the Shadow of Death. The book is written in plain, vigorous English and draws on Bunyan's reading of the Bible and Puritan theology. A second part, following Christian's wife and children, was published in 1684.

books.title: Knowing God
books.author: J.I. Packer
books.description: An exploration of the attributes of God and what it means to know God personally, written from within the Reformed evangelical tradition.
books.longDescription: J.I. Packer published Knowing God in 1973. The book is organized around the question of what it means to know God, drawing on Scripture, the Westminster Catechism, and the broader Reformed tradition. Packer examines God's attributes–his wisdom, justice, mercy, and sovereignty–and discusses how knowledge of God should shape Christian life. The work has been read widely within evangelical and Reformed churches.

books.title: Celebration of Discipline
books.subtitle: The Path to Spiritual Growth
books.author: Richard Foster
books.description: An introduction to the classical spiritual disciplines–meditation, prayer, fasting, study, and others–drawing on historical Christian practice across traditions.
books.longDescription: Richard Foster published Celebration of Discipline in 1978. The book surveys three categories of spiritual disciplines: inward (meditation, prayer, fasting), outward (simplicity, solitude, submission), and corporate (confession, worship, guidance). Foster draws on sources from the Desert Fathers to the Quakers, presenting the disciplines as accessible pathways rather than ascetic obligations. The work is associated with the Renovaré movement.

books.title: The City of God
books.author: Augustine of Hippo
books.edition: Penguin Classics edition, translated by Henry Bettenson, 2003
books.description: A work of historical theology contrasting the earthly city with the City of God, written in response to the sack of Rome in 410 AD.
books.longDescription: Augustine composed The City of God between 413 and 426 AD. The work arose in response to the claim that Rome's fall was caused by the abandonment of pagan gods. Augustine constructs a theology of history, distinguishing between the earthly city (motivated by self-love) and the City of God (motivated by love of God). The twenty-two books range over Roman history, pagan philosophy, and biblical interpretation. The work influenced medieval political thought and the theology of both Catholic and Protestant traditions.

books.title: The Problem of Pain
books.author: C.S. Lewis
books.description: A philosophical and theological examination of how an omnipotent and loving God might permit human suffering.
books.longDescription: C.S. Lewis published The Problem of Pain in 1940. The book addresses the question of theodicy–how to reconcile God's goodness with the existence of suffering. Lewis approaches the topic from a philosophical perspective, drawing on his background in philosophy and English literature. He examines concepts such as divine omnipotence, human free will, and the nature of heaven and hell. The work predates Lewis's own experience of bereavement, which he later explored in A Grief Observed.

books.title: Desiring God
books.subtitle: Meditations of a Christian Hedonist
books.author: John Piper
books.description: An argument that the pursuit of joy in God is not selfish but is, in Piper's framework, the highest calling of humanity and the essence of Christian faith.
books.longDescription: John Piper published Desiring God in 1986, with a revised edition in 2011. The book presents the concept of 'Christian hedonism'–the idea that God is most glorified when humans find their deepest satisfaction in him. Piper draws on Jonathan Edwards, the Puritans, and the Bible to argue that pleasure in God is both a duty and a delight. The work has been influential within Reformed and Baptist circles.

books.title: Institutes of the Christian Religion
books.author: John Calvin
books.description: A systematic presentation of Christian doctrine organized around the Apostles' Creed, first published in 1536 and expanded through four editions.
books.longDescription: John Calvin first published the Institutes in 1536 as a brief introduction to Christian doctrine. The final edition of 1559, organized into four books corresponding to the Apostles' Creed, is the basis for most English translations. Calvin addresses the knowledge of God as Creator and Redeemer, the nature of salvation, the role of the church, and the means of grace. The work has been central to Reformed theology and has influenced Protestant thought broadly.

books.title: The Imitation of Christ
books.author: Thomas à Kempis
books.edition: Penguin Classics edition, translated by Leo Sherley-Price, 1952
books.description: A devotional work in four books on the spiritual life, composed in the early fifteenth century within the Augustinian tradition.
books.longDescription: Thomas à Kempis composed The Imitation of Christ around 1418–1427. The work is divided into four books: on the spiritual life, on the inward life, on consolation, and on the sacrament of the altar. Written in a meditative style, it draws on Scripture and the Church Fathers. The Imitation has been translated into numerous languages and has been read across Catholic, Protestant, and Orthodox traditions.

books.title: Orthodoxy
books.author: G.K. Chesterton
books.description: An account of how Chesterton came to hold the Christian faith, written as a personal defense of his philosophy of life.
books.longDescription: G.K. Chesterton published Orthodoxy in 1908. Rather than constructing a formal apologetic, Chesterton describes the process by which his search for a worldview led him to Christianity. The book engages with contemporary philosophies of the late Victorian period and uses paradox and humor as rhetorical tools. Chesterton later converted to Roman Catholicism in 1922; Orthodoxy reflects his faith during his Anglican period.

books.title: Life Together
books.author: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
books.description: A reflection on Christian community based on Bonhoeffer's experience leading the underground seminary at Finkenwalde during the Nazi era.
books.longDescription: Dietrich Bonhoeffer published Life Together in 1939. The book draws on his experience leading a clandestine seminary in Finkenwalde, Pomerania (now Poland). Bonhoeffer examines the nature of Christian community through five sections: the community of the cross, the community of the Spirit, the community of fellowship, the ministry of service, and the ministry of proclamation. He warns against idealizing fellowship and emphasizes the role of Scripture and the reality of Christ's presence in the community.

books.title: Prayer: Experiencing Awe and Intimacy with God
books.author: Timothy Keller
books.description: A theological and practical exploration of Christian prayer, drawing on historical sources from the Puritans to the early Church.
books.longDescription: Timothy Keller published Prayer in 2014. The book is divided into four sections: the necessity of prayer, the pattern of prayer (drawing on the Lord's Prayer), the life of prayer, and the powers of prayer. Keller draws on sources including Jonathan Edwards, John Owen, the early Church Fathers, and the Reformers. He presents prayer as both a conversation with God and a transformation of the self. The work is written from a Reformed perspective but engages broadly with the Christian tradition.
